records.name: Frontier Nagaland Territorial Authority (FNTA)
records.decision_basis: The amended Bill's passage on 3 September 2026 is now verified in an official Assembly bulletin reproduced in the fully retrieved 30 September Gazette. The final assented Act and commencement/constitution instruments were not verified. The public archive ends at 30 September and other official registers have demonstrably incomplete coverage. Retain the exact hold; do not convert this into nonexistence, exclusion, or a proven pre-operative Act.
confirmed_findings: The 5 February 2026 tripartite agreement is confirmed by the Union Home Ministry; an agreement is not the assented state Act or its commencement instrument.
Confirmed: official 15 September Gazette, Part V, notification AS/LEG-22/Bill/FNTA/2026/298 of 1 September 2026.
Confirmed: 3 September 2026 Assembly bulletin, items 11–13, including the preamble amendment and unanimous passage.
remaining_authority_instruments: Assented final Frontier Nagaland Territorial Authority Act, 2026, or an authenticated official publication identifying its Act number and assent date together with the final text.
Official Gazette commencement notification under the final Act, including any different dates for individual provisions, and the constitution/establishment order if separately required.
currentness_and_access_limits: No verified assent date, Act number or commencement date is supplied. A Bill containing the future short title Act, 2026 is not itself an assented Act.
Do not mark the institution pre-operative merely because commencement was not found: proof of final enactment and noncommencement would be needed for that narrower lifecycle conclusion.
The Gazette cover and bounded searches do not prove no extraordinary or unpublished-to-this-archive instrument exists.
Statements by ministers, newspapers calling it an Act, the political agreement and proposed interim selections do not substitute for the exact legal instruments.
Eligibility in force, establishment/constitution, elections/current operation and broadcast readiness are separate findings. No downstream validation started.

records.name: Consejo General Pueblo Bribri
records.decision_basis: Retain a specific authority evidence hold. Government identifies the Council and Bulú as distinct offices; fieldwork records clan-consensus decisions. Participatory 2025 plans include land-use/conservation rules and strengthen the Council. Generic law respects traditional authority, but its specific allocation cannot be inferred from a title application or development-plan report. The current congress-level allocation of general binding norm-making, financial approval and executive accountability is not established by the instruments obtained; neither eligibility nor an ordinary-local/cultural-only exclusion is justified.

records.name: Congreso General Buglé
records.decision_basis: This is a separately recognised traditional organism, not merely an alias or typo for the already eligible joint comarca congress. Its own presidency is separate from the joint comarca cacicazgo; the consultation record distinguishes both delegations. Recognition for CONDIPI and COONAPIP establishes representation, not a separate autonomous legislative jurisdiction. The adopted Buglé-specific regulation/statute, commencement and defined territorial application were not found. The evidence does not establish independent binding territorial norm-making or budget/executive control; joint-comarca Charter powers cannot supply these missing allocations.

records.name: Congreso General Guna Dagargunyala
records.decision_basis: The 2025 decree’s Tagarkunyala wording and 2018 COONAPIP Dagargunyala wording concern the separately recognised ancestral-territory Congress; identity is no longer an undefined generic Guna lead. The 2020 judgment ties Tagarkunyal’s collective-territory claim to Púcuro and Paya in Darién; the 2026 Guna Congress notice independently identifies a separate leadership. The ministry describes a customary territorial structure distinct from the three statutory Guna comarcas and its two local sagladuras. Number of communities alone does not decide regional-autonomy eligibility. No complete Congress-specific customary statute, territorial normative code or operative resolutions showing binding rules and financial/executive accountability were recovered. The 2020 land judgment leaves the ANATI adjudication outside its decision; it neither grants nor denies legislature status. No current title or parliamentary status is inferred.
